report.source_text:
Immediate treatment with calcium gluconate and magnesium sulphate intravenously was given in the emergency department while monitoring the patient’s heart. Quickly after administration of calcium, his voice improved.
We admitted the patient to the acute care unit where he continued to receive calcium intravenously together with alphacalcidol (1 μg) since his blood test showed hypoparathyroidism and cholecalciferol orally to restore his vitamin D concentration. After 24 hours, he received 20 mmol calcium in total, which resulted in plasma calcium of 1.57 mmol/L (reference range: 2.20–2.65 mmol/L) and a normal QTc interval. He was transferred to the hospital ward where he continued to receive calcium (10 mmol/24 hours) intravenously and alphacalcidol (1 ug) orally. After 5 days, his plasma calcium normalised (2.15 mmol/L) together with normalisation of his creatine kinase level, and he was discharged.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 29-year-old man presented with 3 months of progressively worsening speechlessness, hoarseness, dyspnoea, vomiting after cold water, and hand spasms/cramps, along with positive Chvostek's and Trousseau's signs. Initial blood tests revealed severe hypocalcemia (1.03 mmol/L), raised phosphate (2.21 mmol/L), and low magnesium (0.58 mmol/L), with normal kidney and liver function. Subsequent tests showed low parathyroid hormone (0.7 pmol/L) and low 25-hydroxy(OH)-vitamin D3 (11 nmol). An ECG showed a prolonged QTc interval (501 ms). Further investigations ruled out mutations of the calcium-sensing receptor and parathyroid antibodies. No history of neck surgery or other relevant medical/family history was reported. The patient was treated with intravenous calcium gluconate and magnesium sulphate, followed by intravenous calcium and oral alphacalcidol and cholecalciferol. His symptoms improved, calcium levels normalized, and QTc interval normalized, leading to discharge after 5 days.

Normal kidney and liver function tests were found, ruling out renal causes of electrolyte imbalance.

Patient showed clinical improvement and normalization of calcium levels and QTc interval with calcium and vitamin D supplementation.
